fix(proc): the update act outlives the daemon, and a downed lifeline stands as a warning (brandon-unfiled-3248.86ga)

High review of the lifeline:

- The update act rewrites the bundle, so any daemon exit now killed it
  half-written. A waited launch can say it outlives its launcher, and the
  act does; the binary watch still holds the restart while it runs.
- Why the lifeline is down is one state: the log says each change, and the
  daemon shows it beside the file-events warning, so a broken lifeline
  reaches the bar instead of only daemon.log.
- awk is found on the launcher's PATH, as every launched program is, so a
  machine without /usr/bin/awk (NixOS) is guarded.
- The binary watch says its wait once, through the shared change logger.
- The demo shim's resident programs are programs that answer RESIDENT, one
  registry instead of two.

fix(proc): a launch child dies with the process that launched it, SIGKILL included (brandon-unfiled-3248.86ga)

A launch child leads its own process group, and everything that ended it
(its timeout, its caller's abort, its own exit) ran inside the launcher.
A daemon that exited left every in-flight group running, reparented to
init for good, and a SIGKILL runs no cleanup to prevent that.

Each launching process now starts one lifeline: an awk program in its
own group, reading a pipe only the launcher holds. Every waited child is
registered on it and deregistered when it settles. When the launcher
ends, however it ends, the kernel closes the pipe, and the lifeline sends
the remaining groups the timeout's own escalation: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL
after the grace. The in-process set of live groups is the truth. A lost
lifeline is logged, and the next launch replaces it and hands it the
whole set.

The binary watch now holds a restart while the update notice's act is
running. That act is a launch child rewriting the bundle the watch
samples, and a restart in the middle would now kill it half-written.

The Pages site's child_process shim gains resident programs, since the
lifeline lives as long as the page's daemon.
fix(config): a cell-caused issue refuses only that cell, every restaging preset carries its judged tree, and an id-less cell is satisfied by any placement of its segment (candybar-plugins-vf6g.99v)

fix(config): an inserted cell hides with its anchor, only a preset a cell lands in is rewritten, and each missed entry warns once (candybar-plugins-vf6g.99v)

The unused-declaration report reads the trees with inserts placed, so a
segment only an insert entry places is used. A cell spliced beside an anchor
inside a container carries the anchor's when, as a row anchor's cell is
gated by the row. A preset no cell lands in keeps the fragment it was
written as. One entry that misses several trees is one notice naming them
all. Edit mode's label names the inserting file by its directory and name.

(candybar-plugins-vf6g.99v)

fix(config): the loader places every layer's insert cells once, and the merged config holds none (candybar-plugins-vf6g.99v)

Insert cells were a second carrier of placements on the merged config,
re-placed by every walk of a preset's tree, including over trees the load
had already pruned. The loader now places every layer's cells once, into the
config's root and each restaging preset's tree, before cross-ref and
synthesis, and collects the missed-anchor notices from that same pass.

- A cell naming an undeclared segment is dropped and reported at the
  writing file's insert.<i>, from any layer, instead of crashing edit chrome.
- An anchor on the bar's own chrome is refused at parse, like a chrome seg.
- An inserted cell's names-view label is keyed by preset, so it no longer
  overwrites another preset's editable label of the same id.
- A numeric path part indexes only arrays; on an object the key scanner
  places it as before.
- Insert validation looks up a line only for an issue.
- Docs: an inserted cell is an insert entry, which clicks don't rewrite,
  in any file.
fix(config): an insert cell warns only where a config file wrote the tree it missed (candybar-plugins-vf6g.99v)
fix(config): every rendered tree places a layer's insert cells, so presets decide their own anchors and clashes (candybar-plugins-vf6g.99v)
feat(config): a repo config can add a cell beside a placement the user already has (candybar-plugins-vf6g.99v)

fix(ci): the committed schema has one writer, and the Test job fails a PR that leaves it stale (brandon-unfiled-3248.oq80) (#487)

* fix(ci): the committed schema has one writer, and the Test job fails a PR that leaves it stale (brandon-unfiled-3248.oq80)

The build ran gen-schema before tsdown, so every CI and release run
rewrote schema/cc-candybar.schema.json before anything compared it. The
prepublishOnly check compared the file with a copy the build had just
written, test/config-schema.test.ts read that same copy, and the
committed file on main (the one editors fetch through $id) drifted with
nothing to catch it.

The build no longer regenerates the schema; `pnpm gen:schema` is the
only writer. The required Test job runs check:schema before Build. The
schema is regenerated to match the loader, which adds the look names.

* fix(ci): the schema guard names gen:schema as the truth and lets a read error speak for itself (brandon-unfiled-3248.oq80)

The stale message named only the loader schemas, but the artifact also
carries the bundled default's segment names. A bare catch relabelled every
read error as "missing"; readFileSync's own error is the accurate one.
cli.ts no longer calls the artifact build-generated.
